html:
Grilling shrimp can be a little tricky—tiny pieces slip through the grates, and delicate flesh can dry out quickly. Using a non‑stick BBQ grill mat solves both problems, giving you a smooth surface that keeps the shrimp from falling apart while still delivering that coveted smoky flavor. Below are three easy grilled shrimp recipes that showcase the versatility of a grill mat, plus practical tips for mastering perfect shrimp every time.

Why a Grill Mat Is a Game‑Changer for Grilled Shrimp on a Grill Mat

When you place shrimp directly on the grill bars, they often slide into the gaps, leading to loss of flavor and unwanted flare‑ups from marinades. A reusable non‑stick grill mat creates a continuous cooking surface, preventing shrimp from slipping and allowing any sugary or oily marinades to caramelize without causing flare‑ups. The mat also protects the grates from scratches, making cleanup a breeze and extending the life of your grill.

Essential Prep Tips Before You Start

Before you fire up the grill, follow these quick steps to ensure your shrimp turn out juicy and flavorful:

  1. Pat the shrimp dry. Moisture is the enemy of a good sear; use paper towels to remove excess liquid.
  2. Season early. Toss the shrimp in salt, pepper, and any desired aromatics at least 15 minutes before grilling.
  3. Preheat the grill mat. Place the BBQ Grill Mats on the preheated grill for 2–3 minutes; this helps achieve a quick sear.
  4. Oil the mat lightly. A thin brush of high‑smoke‑point oil (like avocado) prevents sticking while preserving the non‑stick surface.

Recipe 1: Lemon‑Garlic Butter Shrimp

This classic combination is bright, buttery, and perfect for a quick weeknight dinner.

  • 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
  • 2 Tbsp melted butter
  • 1 Tbsp fresh lemon juice
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • ¼ tsp smoked paprika
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • Chopped parsley for garnish

Mix butter, lemon juice, garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Toss the shrimp until evenly coated. Spread the shrimp in a single layer on the preheated BBQ Grill Mats and grill for 2‑3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Finish with a sprinkle of parsley and serve over rice or tossed with a simple salad.

Recipe 2: Spicy Coconut‑Lime Shrimp

For a tropical twist with a kick, this recipe uses coconut milk and a touch of chili.

  • 1 lb shrimp
  • ½ cup coconut milk
  • 1 Tbsp lime zest
  • 1 Tbsp lime juice
  • 1 tsp chili flakes (adjust to heat preference)
  • 1 Tbsp soy sauce
  • 1 Tbsp honey

Combine coconut milk, lime zest, lime juice, chili flakes, soy sauce, and honey. Marinate the shrimp for 20 minutes, then drain excess liquid. Place the shrimp on the BBQ Grill Mats and grill 2‑4 minutes per side. The coconut coating creates a subtle caramelized crust while the lime adds fresh acidity. Serve with cilantro and a side of quinoa.

Recipe 3: Herb‑Crusted Shrimp Skewers

Skewers make turning and serving a breeze, and the grill mat ensures the herb crust stays intact.

  • 1 lb shrimp
  • 2 Tbsp olive oil
  • 1 Tbsp dried oregano
  • 1 Tbsp dried thyme
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • Salt and pepper
  • Wooden or metal skewers (soaked if wooden)

Thread three shrimp onto each skewer. Brush with olive oil, then sprinkle the herb mixture, salt, and pepper. Lay the skewers on the BBQ Grill Mats and grill for about 3 minutes per side, rotating once. The herbs form a fragrant crust that stays on the shrimp thanks to the non‑stick surface. Pair with a cucumber‑yogurt dip for a summer‑ready appetizer.

Cleaning and Maintaining Your BBQ Grill Mats

After the last shrimp is devoured, let the mat cool, then scrape off any food remnants with a silicone spatula. Rinse with warm, soapy water and a non‑abrasive scrubber. For stubborn char, a soak in a mixture of water and a few drops of dish soap for 15 minutes does the trick. Once clean, dry thoroughly and store flat or rolled to keep the mat ready for the next grill session.

FAQ

Can I use the grill mat on a charcoal grill?

Absolutely. The mat is heat‑resistant up to 500°F, making it safe for both gas and charcoal grills. Just place it directly on the hot coals after they have burned down to an even heat.

Will the non‑stick coating wear off after repeated use?

The BBQ Grill Mats are designed for repeated use. As long as you avoid metal utensils and abrasive cleaners, the coating will remain functional for many grilling seasons.

Do I need to oil the mat before every use?

A light brush of high‑smoke‑point oil each time helps maintain the non‑stick surface and enhances flavor, especially for delicate items like shrimp.
